question: What is another common medical name for a pressure sore?
explanation: Pressure sores are frequently referred to as decubitus ulcers due to their tendency to form while lying down. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do pressure sores develop primarily over bony prominences?

options.A: Tissue is trapped between bone and a hard surface
options.B: Skin is thinner and lacks sweat glands there
options.C: Bone presses outward against external surfaces
options.D: Blood flow is naturally absent in those areas

explanation: External pressure compresses soft tissue against the underlying skeleton, cutting off capillary blood supply. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which body area is most at risk when a patient lies flat on their back?
explanation: The sacrum bears a large amount of body weight when a patient is in the supine position. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: A patient spending hours in a wheelchair is most likely to develop a sore on the...
explanation: Sitting puts direct weight and pressure squarely on the ischial tuberosities of the pelvis. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: What happens during a shearing force injury?

options.A: Sweat softens the skin barrier against the mattress
options.B: Friction removes the top layer of dry epidermal skin cells
options.C: Skin and bone slide in opposite directions, twisting blood vessels
options.D: Direct body weight completely stops all venous blood return

explanation: Shear occurs when skeletal structures move downward while friction holds the outer skin fixed, stretching local blood vessels. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which factor directly lowers the structural resilience of skin against pressure?
explanation: Inadequate nutrient intake deprives skin and soft tissues of the building blocks needed to maintain strength and repair damage. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: How is a Stage 1 pressure injury best identified on a patient with light skin?
explanation: Stage 1 is marked by redness that does not turn white when you press your finger against the skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is a pressure sore classified as unstageable?

options.A: Dead tissue covers the base so true depth is hidden
options.B: Infection has destroyed the surrounding anatomical landmarks
options.C: The wound has healed over but left a permanent scar
options.D: It is caused by moisture rather than physical pressure

explanation: Slough or eschar blocks the view of the wound bed, preventing the nurse from determining how deep the damage goes. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which solution is safest for routine cleansing of an open pressure sore?
explanation: Normal saline is isotonic and cleans the wound without harming newly forming granulation tissue. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of debridement in pressure sore management?

options.A: Drying out excess moisture in deep craters
options.B: Stopping minor bleeding from surface capillaries
options.C: Removing dead tissue to allow healthy healing
options.D: Sealing the wound shut against external bacteria

explanation: Necrotic tissue acts as a barrier to healing and a breeding ground for bacteria, so it must be cleared away. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the standard frequency for turning a bedbound patient to prevent pressure sores?
explanation: Repositioning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable capillaries. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: How do barrier creams assist in pressure sore prevention?

options.A: They harden the epidermis against sharp shear forces
options.B: They increase local blood circulation in deep muscles
options.C: They shield skin from moisture and chemical irritation
options.D: They replace the need for regular patient repositioning

explanation: Barrier creams create a hydrophobic layer that stops urine and sweat from breaking down the skin barrier. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)
